sourcedFrom: Uberti Single Action Revolver and Revolving Carbine Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code or revision is printed on the leaflet (undated — no copyright line is printed)
cleanIntro: Uberti's own single-action book, which names this gun in its parts-list heading as the 1873 S.A. CATTLEMAN. There is no slide and no takedown lever here — the whole strip is getting the cylinder out through the loading gate, and the base pin is the only thing holding it in.

steps.title: Hammer to half cock, gate open, every chamber checked
steps.action: Point it somewhere safe, draw the hammer back to half cock and open the loading gate on the right rear of the frame. At half cock the cylinder turns freely, so rotate it a full six and look into each chamber in turn. A single-action shows you one chamber at a time through the gate — the gun is not clear because the one you can see is.
steps.aside: Close the loading gate after you are sure that all six chambers in your revolver are empty.
steps.quote: Draw the hammer to its half-cock position and open the loading gate on the right rear part of the frame.
steps.cite: Uberti Single Action Revolver and Revolving Carbine Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code or revision is printed on the leaflet — UNLOADING, p.1 (single-page leaflet, no printed folio)

steps.title: Ejector rod driven full stroke, not part way
steps.action: Push each case out with the ejector rod under the barrel, and run the rod its whole travel every time. A short stroke lifts the case out of the chamber mouth but leaves it in the frame window where it jams the cylinder on the next turn. Work round all six even if you think it came out empty.
steps.aside: Operate the ejector rod in each chamber to its full length to assure full length  case ejection.
steps.quote: Push out each cartridge or empty case with the ejector rod located under the barrel.
steps.cite: Uberti Single Action Revolver and Revolving Carbine Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code or revision is printed on the leaflet — UNLOADING, p.1

steps.title: Which safety your gun has — this book covers more than one
steps.action: Before going further, find out which safety is fitted, because Uberti builds this line both ways and the book branches on it. Look at the rear of the hammer: a small slot there means a hammer block safety. No slot means the safety lives in an elongated cylinder base pin instead, and that version splits again between an old-model black powder frame and a pre-war or new model frame. Nothing on the outside of the box tells you — the gun does.
steps.aside: These guns have an elongated cylinder base pin, with two safety positions that function as a hammer safety block on both models, old model frame (black powder) and new model frame (pre-war, modern).
steps.quote: These guns have a hammer block safety in the hammer. If you see a small slot at the rear of the hammer, then your hammer has a safety already inserted.
steps.cite: Uberti Single Action Revolver and Revolving Carbine Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code or revision is printed on the leaflet — A - BASIC SAFETY, “AT REST” AND “TRANSPORT POSITION”, p.1
steps.warn: Every model has a safety (first cock position) machined into the hammer. This is a voluntary safety and not an automatic safety;

steps.title: Confirmed empty, then gate open and hammer at half cock again
steps.action: Uberti restates both conditions at the head of the cleaning strip, and they are the two that make the cylinder free to come out: the loading gate open so there is somewhere for it to go, and the hammer at its half-cock notch so the bolt drops out of the cylinder notches. Try it at full cock or with the gate shut and the cylinder will not clear the frame.
steps.aside: Put the hammer in its half-cock notch.
steps.quote: Check first to make sure your revolver is empty. Then remove the cylinder using the following steps:
steps.cite: Uberti Single Action Revolver and Revolving Carbine Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code or revision is printed on the leaflet — CLEANING, opening line, p.1

steps.title: Base pin catch held in, on the left front of the frame
steps.action: Find the spring-loaded plunger on the left front side of the frame, just ahead of the cylinder, and press it in. Keep it pressed — this is not a push-and-release. It is a detent bearing on a groove in the base pin, and the moment you let go it drops back in and locks the pin where it sits.
steps.quote: Depress the base pin catch. This is the spring loaded plunger which is located on the left front side of the frame. Keep it depressed.
steps.cite: Uberti Single Action Revolver and Revolving Carbine Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code or revision is printed on the leaflet — CLEANING, step 3, p.1

steps.title: Base pin drawn all the way forward and out
steps.action: With the catch still held, pull the base pin forward and out of the frame. It has to come the whole way — part way out still leaves it through the cylinder. This is the pin the cylinder actually turns on, so treat its surface as a bearing rather than as a bolt: it wants to be clean and lightly oiled, not dry and not gritty.
steps.quote: Slide the base pin all the way out. The base pin is the heavy pin around which the cylinder revolves (and provides a bearing surface for the cylinder). It should always be clean and lubricated.
steps.cite: Uberti Single Action Revolver and Revolving Carbine Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code or revision is printed on the leaflet — CLEANING, step 4, p.1

steps.title: Cylinder out sideways, through the open gate
steps.action: Roll the cylinder out of the frame window toward the loading gate — that open gate is the doorway, which is why it was opened first. It is a close fit and it is meant to be. If it hangs up, stop and check the hammer is still at half cock and the gate fully open rather than leaning on it.
steps.caution: The cylinder is made to fit your revolver precisely and can be removed and replaced  easily, but carefully. It is a close fit, so don’t force it to move in any direction.
steps.quote: Remove cylinder toward the loading gate.
steps.cite: Uberti Single Action Revolver and Revolving Carbine Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code or revision is printed on the leaflet — CLEANING, step 5, p.1

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Cylinder and base pin are off the frame, and that is the whole strip Uberti publishes for this revolver. The book takes it no further — no hammer, no hand, no bolt, no springs — so nothing below that line is documented here. Clean what you have and put it back the way it came apart.
steps.quote: To reassemble, simply reverse the steps used in removal.
steps.cite: Uberti Single Action Revolver and Revolving Carbine Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code or revision is printed on the leaflet — CLEANING, reassembly note, p.1
steps.warn: NEVER use cartridges marked “High Speed” or “High Velocity”.

deepAbsentReason: Uberti's single-action leaflet publishes exactly one disassembly: the five-step cylinder removal under CLEANING. Beyond that it prints a numbered parts list (1 FRAME through 692 HAND PIN SCREW) and nothing else — no procedure for the backstrap, trigger guard, main spring, hand, bolt or the hammer safety bar, all of which the parts list names. A parts list is an identification aid, not a teardown, so no deeper procedure was invented from it. The book's own instruction on the one thing it does document is that the fit is close and must not be forced, which is the opposite of a licence to go further.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBERS
tasks: Scrub the bore and every chamber with a good cleaning solution, using a wood, aluminium or brass rod — never steel
Push the brush all the way through before reversing; never change direction with the brush inside the bore or a chamber
Run clean patches through bore and chambers until they come out clean

cleaning.name: BASE PIN & FRAME WINDOW
tasks: Wipe the base pin down its whole length and lightly oil it — it is the cylinder's bearing surface
Clean the base pin hole and the frame window, including the recoil shield and the face behind the gate
Wipe the cylinder's ratchet face and the front face where it meets the barrel

cleaning.name: OUTSIDE & BRASS
tasks: Oil the whole revolver completely but lightly once it is clean and dry
Bring the brass backstrap and trigger guard back with a good brass polish
Wipe the one-piece grip rather than soaking it

reassembly: Roll the cylinder back into the frame window from the loading gate side, hammer still at half cock.
Slide the base pin back through the frame and the cylinder until it seats fully forward.
Make sure the base pin catch snaps back to its regular position rather than being left riding on the pin.
Test the catch: press the plunger and confirm it moves freely and returns under its own spring pressure.
Close the loading gate and lower the hammer to its safety notch position.
fncheck: With the revolver confirmed empty, press the base pin catch and confirm it springs back on its own — that is Uberti's own published check that the pin is locked in. Then open the gate, bring the hammer to half cock and confirm the cylinder turns freely and the bolt drops into each notch as it comes round, and finally confirm the hammer reaches its safety notch and its full cock notch cleanly. Never squeeze the trigger anywhere but full cock: the book warns that doing so strains the mechanism.
